claims.text: Elemental Cr coatings are applied to zirconium-alloy fuel cladding as protective coatings.
The conventional elemental Cr-coated baseline has no interlayer between the Cr and zirconium alloy.
The proposed intervention is a 50–100 nm ALD-deposited Al2O3 interlayer between the zirconium-alloy substrate and Cr coating.
Optimization of ALD deposition temperature, cycle count, and precursor selection can produce continuous and adherent Al2O3 coverage.
A 50–100 nm ALD Al2O3 interlayer will be robust and conformal.
The Al2O3 interlayer will prevent premature Cr-coating failure caused by Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Approximately 350°C subcritical water represents the targeted normal-operation environment.
Accident-relevant exposure includes high-temperature steam up to approximately 1200°C for seconds to minutes.
A dense Al2O3 interlayer will physically and chemically maintain separation between Cr and the zirconium substrate.
Al2O3 has extremely low ionic and atomic diffusivity and excellent chemical inertness under the proposed conditions.
The Al2O3 interlayer will inhibit elevated-temperature diffusion of Cr and Zr atoms.
The interlayer will eliminate or severely restrict high-diffusivity pathways at the Cr/Zr interface.
Restricting Cr–Zr interdiffusion will prevent formation of detrimental intermetallic phases.
Preventing interdiffusion and intermetallic formation will preserve the protective integrity of the Cr coating.
Relative to the unmodified Cr-coated baseline, the Al2O3-interlayered system will exhibit a significantly lower Cr–Zr interdiffusion rate.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion will prolong coating integrity and improve corrosion resistance in both approximately 350°C subcritical water and short high-temperature steam exposures.
The unmodified Cr-coated zirconium-alloy baseline is prone to premature degradation from elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Cr is among the metallic coatings investigated to improve high-temperature oxidation resistance of zirconium-alloy cladding.
